title: User profile errors
executive_summary: user-service error rate rose from ~0.4% to ~30% and timeout rate from ~0.05% to ~9% starting 21:03Z, five minutes into the T0 window. Logs show repeated "connection refused" and "connection reset by peer" errors to postgres-primary:5432. One kernel conntrack "table full, dropping packet" warning was logged on usr-node-3 at 21:02Z, one minute before onset. The database itself shows no clear saturation at onset, and its telemetry is missing from 21:00 onward. The most likely cause is a connection-layer failure between user-service nodes and the database, probably related to the conntrack exhaustion on usr-node-3. This is not confirmed: the per-node error breakdown and network-level data are missing.

hypotheses.description: Connection tracking table exhaustion on user-service node usr-node-3 causes dropped/reset TCP sessions to postgres, producing intermittent connection-refused and reset errors. Mechanism: nf_conntrack table fills at ~21:02, new connections from usr-node-3 are dropped or reset; the pool retries (attempt counters up to 91) and requests time out, raising error and timeout rates in user-service.

hypotheses.description: Long-running report_rollup() queries on postgres saturate the primary, causing connection acceptance failures and resets for user-service. Mechanism: report_rollup() runs for 11-20 seconds from 20:50 onward, holding resources and possibly exhausting connection slots or backend processes, so new connections are refused or reset.

probable_root_cause.description: Connection tracking table exhaustion on user-service node usr-node-3 causes dropped/reset TCP sessions to postgres, producing intermittent connection-refused and reset errors.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): infrastructure_degradation in user-service - Connection tracking table exhaustion on user-service node usr-node-3 causes dropped/reset TCP sessions to postgres, producing intermittent connection-refused and reset errors.
corrective_actions: Check nf_conntrack usage on all user-service nodes, especially usr-node-3, and raise nf_conntrack_max or drain and restart the affected node if it is full.
Confirm whether errors are concentrated on usr-node-3 and fail over or drain that node from the load balancer.
Verify postgres-primary accepts connections from user-service and that max_connections is not exceeded.
preventive_actions: Alert on conntrack table utilisation above 80% on all service nodes.
Move the report_rollup() job off the primary or bound its runtime.
Fix the metrics-agent export backlog so database telemetry is not lost during incidents.
monitoring_recommendations: Track nf_conntrack count vs max per node, and user-service error rate and timeout rate per node.
Track postgres connection counts and rollup query duration, with alerts on any gap in postgres telemetry.
Monitor user-service connection refused and reset counts by node.
limitations: Errors and telemetry may have been delayed by the metrics-agent backlog.
The conntrack warning is a single log line and is not proof of causation.
Temporal correlation between the 21:02 conntrack warning and the 21:03 onset is not causation.
[agent-reported gap] Telemetry for postgres is missing for 31 of 56 datapoints from 21:00 onward; query_metrics returned postgres as a service, but timeout_rate is not collected for it.
[agent-reported gap] The query for 'postgres-primary' failed because it is not a known service name. The database is registered as 'postgres'.
[agent-reported gap] No per-node breakdown of user-service errors.
[agent-reported gap] No network or conntrack utilisation metrics beyond one log line.
[agent-reported gap] Historical incident search was not run.
2 tool calls failed and 0 returned partial data; affected areas are treated as unknown, not healthy.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely cause is a connection-layer failure between user-service and postgres starting 21:03Z. The best candidate is conntrack exhaustion on usr-node-3 (H1), but the evidence is limited: one warning on one node, no per-node error breakdown, and no network metrics. Postgres-side saturation from report_rollup (H2) is less likely because connection utilisation stayed normal in the available telemetry. No deployment or configuration change was recorded in the window. Final status is PROBABLE, not ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED.
